title: Actor definition
description: One file per actor kind. An actor is a name over stored state with a durable mailbox. Its behaviour is the list of receive clauses: given the current state and one input (a stored message, or the unstored tick carrying evidence), the first clause whose `in`, `on` and `when` all hold fires; it moves the actor to `to` and appends `effects` to the outbox. Every predicate and effect is an abstract atom name from atoms.yaml; nothing here names a store, a field, a path or a service (requirement 125, invariant I13).

actor.description: the actor kind; also the first segment of every actor id of this kind

version.description: moves when this file's behaviour moves; an actor records the version it started under

supervisor.description: the parent kind in the supervision tree; null only for the org root

lease.description: root: a host takes a lease on this actor and thereby on its whole subtree. inherited: run by whoever holds the nearest root ancestor's lease. self: the actor is its own host record (host kind only).

fields.description: stored attributes of the actor beyond its state; name → type note

decisions.description: the plan row kinds this actor may open. Each is spawned as a `decision` actor whose id is <this actor id>/<kind>[/<key>], so a repeat of the opening effect is a no-op and an answered decision is never re-asked.

key.description: expression over evidence that makes a genuinely new situation a new decision id; absent means one per parent

retracted-by.description: the one retracting condition besides the word itself (invariant I3)

row.description: what the row says, in the plan mockup's words

in.description: state or list of states; '*' for any

on.description: a message kind such as `decided`, `session.exited`, `word.direct`, or a list of kinds; or `tick` (the unstored input carrying evidence)

when.description: predicate atoms, all of which must hold; each is `name(args)` from atoms.yaml evidence

effects.description: effect atoms `name(args)` appended to the outbox in order; ids are <actor>/<seq>/<n>

supervision.description: what this actor does when a child's runtime attachment is lost (its process, its place, its host). State is never lost, so the choices are about the attachment only.

bound.description: atom or type field naming the retry bound
